newsitem.title: USA: IBJ Schroder bank agrees to stay in New York City.
newsitem.headline: IBJ Schroder bank agrees to stay in New York City.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said Friday commercial bank IBJ Schroder Bank & Trust Co, which opened its first office in the city 75 years ago, agreed to remain, retaining 500 jobs.
Further, the bank said it would create as many as 460 new jobs over the 22 year-period that the bank promised to remain, Giuliani said, in prepared remarks.

In return, the bank gets a maximum of about $1 million in sales tax exemptions for tenant improvement work and buying office equipment and machinery. The total benefit package was estimated at about $3.1 million, with the city's share of the sales tax benefits, about $1.1 million, expected to be repaid to the city in tax revenues in about two-and-a-half months.

The bank, whch intended to move to New Jersey if did not get a benefit package, produces about $5.5 million of tax revenues for New York City each year. IBJ Schroder is located at One State Street, and has yet to decide if it will expand its present site or relocate within lower Manhattan when its lease ends in 2001.

Giuliani said his Administration has now kept more than 30 companies from leaving the city, retaining 71,352 jobs, and adding as many as 26,020 new jobs. The total tax revenue generated by the firms for the city is $1.14 billion a year.
